item.title: W3-L2 — The Deadline on the Desk
item.description: This encounter opened with low affective energy. The assessment rubric, distributed the previous week, seemed to weigh on the room. Boredom was visible in the first fifteen minutes — bodies angled away from the board, minimal eye contact with the task. The turn came when S3, seated at the cluster of round tables near the window, held up their laminated rubric and remarked, deadpan: “This looks like something you’d find at a funeral.

item.title: W5-L3 — S3 Hands the Rhizome Back
item.description: S3 arrived before the bell. I watched them rearrange a chair near the window and then, after a moment, replace it exactly as it was. This small act of anticipatory arrangement stayed with me throughout the lesson. The blank whiteboard held the room in a different way from the previous two encounters. No instruction, no deadline — just space. When I asked what students remembered from W4, S3 spoke immediately: “Everything connects to everything and nothing connects to anything.
